label: Just started earning
teaser: First job, first salary — and cover that quietly belongs to your employer, not to you.
headline: You are covered — until the day you resign
intro: Group cover from your employer feels like a solved problem. It is the single most common gap we fix, because it disappears exactly when your income does.

pains.heading: Your group cover ends the day you leave
pains.body: Employer health cover is not portable. It does not follow you to the next job, it does not cover you through a notice period gap, and it ends immediately if you are laid off — which is the exact moment a hospital bill would hurt most.

pains.heading: You have aged off your parents' family floater
pains.body: Most family floaters drop dependent children at 25. Many people discover this at a claim, not at renewal. If nobody has bought you a plan in your own name, you are uninsured and do not know it yet.

pains.heading: Waiting periods only start counting once you buy
pains.body: Every health policy makes you wait 2–3 years before pre-existing and named illnesses are covered. Those years pass whether or not you have a policy — so the cheapest year to start serving them is this one, while you are healthy and premiums are at their lowest.
pains.stat: A 25-year-old pays ₹10,149/yr — the same cover at 45 costs several times more
